What movies do you think are underrated/underappreciated, and what do you appreciate about them?

In other words, why should I watch it? Basically, try to elaborate a bit on your answer a little, instead of just dropping the name of a movie, and leaving it at that. Even just a few sentences. I'm not looking for a novel, but feel free to write one, if you feel the need. I know most of you will still just drop a name and run, but that is alright. I'll deal with it. I am just hoping to spark a bit of conversation.

I should note beforehand that I am judging how underrated I think a movie is based on it's rating on IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes. I figured those sites were my best sources for a general consensus (but I could be wrong).

Some movies I think are underrated, in no particular order:

Transylvania 6-5000 (1985)

Trailer

This movie is terribly underrated. Or maybe I'm just an idiot. The comedy is very much in the style of Mel Brooks's movies (the writer/director, Rudy De Luca, worked with Brooks on at least a couple of movies), so if you enjoy those, you will probably find something to like about this movie. Plus Michael Richards is just great in this, despite how most people feel about him now. He is a fantastic physical comedian. There is one scene (SPOILER ALERT!), which was improvised (according to the DVD commentary) by Richards, in this movie that almost kills me with laughter every time I see it. The other actors had no idea what Richards was going to do, and their reactions show that. Most of Richards lines/scenes were improvised as well, which is awesome.

Explorers (1985)

Trailer

I used to love this movie as a kid, and am surprised more people don't seem to love it like I did. If you like The Goonies, or Flight of the Navigator, you'll probably like this. I always wanted to build a spaceship like the kids in the movie. Plus the trailer is one of my favourite teasers of all time. If you've seen the teaser for Back to the Future, it's kind of similar to that actually (I think they might be directed by the same person). I didn't actually see the teaser for Explorers as a kid, but if I had, I definitely would have wanted to see it.

Dragnet (1987)

Trailer

How this movie only has a rating of 5.9 on IMDb, I'll never know. Used to love this movie as a kid, and still do today. Sure it isn't comedy gold or anything, but it's got plenty of laughs. Plus it's got an awesome accompanying music video, for the soundtrack. What more could you ask for?

The Man with Two Brains (1983)

Trailer

I thought this movie was pretty damn funny. It's possible that I am just easily amused though. It may not be as good as The Jerk, or Dead Men Don't Wear Plaid (which is also underrated), but it's from the same director, so it has a lot of the same style. The trailer doesn't do it justice, so don't judge it by that crap. A solid Steve Martin vehicle.

Parents (1989)

Trailer

I think this one is underrated just because it's mostly unheard of. If you like atmospheric horror movies with a surreal vibe, you may like this. It's got some pretty good cinematography, if you care at all about that, as well as some good acting from the unknown Bryan Madorsky, who plays the kid. I am surprised he didn't go on to do more movies. Plus it's got Randy Quaid, so it's got to be good.

Gummo (1997)

Trailer

This movie is bizarre, grimy, disturbing, and also fairly surreal, and that is why I really like it. I think it's one of those movies that people either love or hate. There is no in-between. I don't claim to understand wtf is going on, or what Harmony Korine is trying to say with this movie, but I still enjoy it. Again, I am drawn to the cinematography, and in this case the documentary style of it. Also really dig the narration by Jacob Reynolds's character, Solomon. It's like audio/visual poetry. I think that trailer is an good example of that. What's it all mean? Beats me, but I still like it.

There are tons more I could list, but I better leave some for other people. That is just a semi-random selection of movies I think are underrated. As you can see, I like movies from the '80s, and my taste is a litte eclectic. I just love movies of all sorts.
